items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains lowest men
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: What qualifications must a recipient meet before receiving this teaching?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Only a previously accomplished person tested for one year is fit to receive it.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one already accomplished, after being tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvipa?
premises: A chapter is being identified
It is the fifth chapter
It belongs to the text emerged from Candradvipa
items.inference: The fifth chapter of the text emerged from Candradvipa concludes here.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvipa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of Kaula become known to the speaker?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The object known is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has understood the determination of Kaula.
items.plain_english: O lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of Kaula.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The verse asks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what reality does the soul dissolve, and can this be fully explained?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
The speaker requests a complete explanation
items.inference: The verse seeks to know where the soul dissolves and asks for a full account.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the reality identified as that soul?
premises: That reality is supreme
That reality is partless and eternal
That reality is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The soul in its highest sense is defined as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to Hamsa and the individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That same soul is identified as Hamsa
It is also called the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as Hamsa, the individual associated with power.
uncertainties: The exact sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed he is the Hamsa, the individual associated with power.

items.question: Where does the breath-filled vital air abide within living beings?
premises: Vital air fills with breath
This air is situated somewhere
Its locus is all living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is unusual in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filling air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the physical body?
premises: The subject leaves the body
This leaving is the decisive condition
The subject is then designated supreme Shiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that soul is called supreme Shiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Shiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted according to the traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes through an ordered lineage
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is heard directly in the ear, having come down through traditional succession.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the traditional lineage.

items.question: What transformative power is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing alone is emphasized
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even mere knowledge, simply heard, is presented as having significant effect.
uncertainties: The sentence continues into the next verse, so the full result is unstated here.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described as one who practices
The result is freedom from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of kāṣāyaṃ is ambiguous in this context.
items.plain_english: If one practices for six months, one becomes free from bondage.

items.question: What social and bodily result follows successful practice of this teaching?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with yogis is presented as an outcome
items.inference: Successful practice results in freedom from disease and communion with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, one attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What specific instruction has now been communicated to Bhairavi?
premises: A teaching has been told
The recipient is Bhairavi
The content is the practice concerning the soul
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavi.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavi, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved person may this teaching rightly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have firm resolve
items.inference: This teaching should be given to a fully endowed person of firm resolve.
uncertainties: The phrase sarva+bhāva+upapannasya admits multiple doctrinal readings.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one endowed with all states and of firm resolve.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginis be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is from the yoginis
Transmission of this essence is prohibited
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginis, must not be given out.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginis, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the speaker's body is claimed after receiving this knowledge?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now declared pure
items.inference: The speaker claims her body, once veiled by ignorance, is now pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now seek to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish concerns hearing a teaching
The teaching concerns the deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious method for overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means for deceiving time.

items.question: What assurance is given regarding the possibility of destroying death?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
No doubt is asserted
Death can be destroyed
items.inference: The teacher assures without doubt that a method will be given by which death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: Who may still suffer burning despite contact with the tip of nectar and essence?
premises: The tip of nectar is mentioned
The essence of juice is present
Even a wise person may be burning
items.inference: Even a wise person can experience burning despite proximity to nectar and essence.
uncertainties: The physiological referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are not explicit.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may burn, though at the tip of nectar with the essence of juice.

items.question: What yogic action at the root of tongue and palate is prescribed for practice?
premises: A specific bodily location is indicated
Air is to be drawn in
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: One should slowly drink the air at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing attention at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink the air.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this method continuously for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The condition of practice is fulfilled
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this method destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for one accomplished in this practice?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the practitioner's body.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
